rules.logic: ABIOC("ITDR-013 dMSA Created Outside Managed Service Accounts Container By Non-Privileged Identity") AND ABIOC("ITDR-013 dMSA Dual Privileged-Attribute Write Lineage In One Logon Session") joined on the same host_name and subject_logon_id within 600 seconds — the create-and-modify pairing shares the attacker's originating logon session (the 5137 creation and both 5136 writes carry one subject_logon_id). That lineage is then joined to XQL("ITDR-013 Hunt dMSA Privileged TGT And Inherited-Privilege Logon") on the created-dMSA IDENTITY, not on subject_logon_id: the sAMAccountName / object_dn of the dMSA created in the 5137 event (websvc-dmsa$) equals the account_name authenticating in the 2946 TGT mint and 4624 logon, which run under the dMSA's OWN new logon session and therefore do NOT carry the attacker's subject_logon_id — within the same 600-second window and host_name. Fuses the create-and-modify dMSA lineage (5137 create -> dual 5136 write under one subject_logon_id) with the privileged-TGT mint (2946) and the inherited-privilege logon (4624) bound by dMSA identity into a single ITDR privilege-escalation incident, evidencing the BadSuccessor storyline end to end.
rules.name: ITDR-013 BadSuccessor dMSA Privilege-Escalation Chain Stitch
